reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Power over AI concentrated in few hands
themes.definition: Concern that a few states or private players concentrate power over AI and computing, deciding the future for others and threatening peoples' sovereignty.
themes.inclusion: Include passages objecting to a few actors, companies, or powers monopolising AI or computational capacity or deciding AI's direction for everyone.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general anti-imperialism statements without reference to AI or computation.
themes.boundary_cases: 'Monopolizing the ability to make calculations' is an oblique compute reference and counts when in a technology context.

examples.quote: We cannot let a few people — let alone private players, who are currently at the forefront of such innovations — think up their future for us and our peoples.
people who believe that they can decide the fate of the planet, whether that be as regards the climate or AI

themes.label: Common ethical democratic AI framework
themes.definition: Calls for coordinated international frameworks for AI, including a united ethical and democratic framework and summit diplomacy to build it.
themes.inclusion: Include calls for Member States to coordinate on AI and build common AI frameworks, including hosting AI summits for that purpose.
themes.exclusion: Exclude security-only cooperation on sensitive AI components (AI_SECURITY_ARMS_CONTROL).
themes.boundary_cases: Praise for the Global Digital Compact alongside a framework call also qualifies for AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: we need all of that to develop within a united ethical and democratic framework, designed by the peoples of the planet
France will be hosting the next Artificial Intelligence Action Summit in February 2025

themes.label: AI in arms-control and security frameworks
themes.definition: AI treated as a new strategic risk alongside nuclear, chemical, cyber, space and quantum threats, requiring arms-control-style frameworks and security cooperation to protect sensitive AI components.
themes.inclusion: Include passages placing AI among proliferation or strategic security risks needing verification or cooperation frameworks, or protecting AI components affecting national security.
themes.exclusion: Exclude explicit autonomous weapons discussions (AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS) and civil governance calls.
themes.boundary_cases: If the passage explicitly discusses AI-enabled weapons or targeting, code AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS instead.

examples.quote: I'm not forgetting bacteriological, chemical threats or the new risks that posed by AI.
We want to set a cooperation agenda on AI so as to protect the most sensitive components thereof, which affect our national security.

themes.label: AI innovation accessible to all
themes.definition: AI innovation must be accessible to all countries and not fuel new divides and inequalities.
themes.inclusion: Include statements that AI access must be universal or that AI must not create new divides.
themes.exclusion: Exclude concentration-of-power framings focused on who controls AI (AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION).
themes.boundary_cases: Statements on North-South unity on technology without AI access are borderline and not coded.

examples.quote: ensure that innovation in artificial intelligence is accessible to all the countries and peoples of the planet and that it does not fuel new divides and inequalities

themes.label: Endorsing Secretary-General's digital work
themes.definition: Praise for the UN Secretary-General's AI-related work, including the Global Digital Compact.
themes.inclusion: Include endorsements of specific UN AI or digital processes.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general support for the UN without AI linkage.
themes.boundary_cases: Calls for UN multilateralism on 'technology' generally are coded only if AI is the subject nearby.

examples.quote: I am delighted with the work that has been carried out and coordinated by the Secretary-General, including on the Global Digital Compact

value.rationale: France's passages frame AI as a question of power and multilateral order: concentrated control by a few, the need for common ethical frameworks and summitry, and AI as a strategic security risk alongside WMD and cyber. Accessibility for all countries is a secondary strand.
